label: Army orders
summary: The orders object of the army shown in the army window.
details: Vanilla only reads its GetHalt part from it, once to show a button, once to check that the command is valid and once to send it when the button is clicked. Going by the name, that command halts the army. It is promoted to a UnitOrders object, so you chain another function after it.

label: Possible commanders text
summary: A text about the commanders that could lead the army in the army window.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it, so what exactly it lists is not shown. The game documents nothing more.

label: Raid intent
summary: The raid intent object that the army window offers.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of a part of the army window, so the widgets inside read their values from it. Going by its name, it is about the army's raiding. Its return type is not registered in the game's data, so what it offers is not documented.

label: Selected unit items
summary: The list of items for the units currently selected in the army window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, so one row is drawn per item. Going by its name, the items are the selected units.

label: Show commanders tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the button that shows the commanders in the army window.
details: Vanilla puts it in the tooltip line of a widget of the army window. Going by its name, that widget is the show-commanders button.

label: Soldier count text
summary: A text with the number of soldiers of the army in the army window.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on the army window. Lines with the same function name on other objects exist (for example on the army entry of the outliner), but they are only a hint.

label: Supply state frame
summary: The frame number of the supply state icon of the army in the army window.
details: Vanilla gives it as the frame of an icon, which picks one picture out of a strip of pictures. Going by its name, the frame depends on the army's supply state.

label: Total soldier count text
summary: A text with the total soldier count of the army in the army window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla only has it in a commented-out line of the army window, so it is not shown in the live game.

label: Troop items
summary: The list of troop items of the army in the army window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list, so one row is drawn per item. Going by its name, the items are troops. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Unit item
summary: The unit item the army window works with.
details: Vanilla reads the status description from it and shows that as text. It is promoted to a UnitItem object, so you chain another function after it.

label: Go to next army
summary: Switches the army window to the next army.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Go to previous army
summary: Switches the army window to the previous army.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Is attached to a unit
summary: Whether the army window is attached to any unit.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the window, often together with CanAttachToMultipleLocalUnits. What attached means is not documented; going by the name, the window is tied to a unit.

label: Merge selected
summary: Merges the selected units of the army window.
details: Going by its name, the selected units are joined into one. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Next army
summary: An action of the army window that goes to the next army.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. The window's buttons use GoToNextArmy instead. It returns nothing.

label: No commander click
summary: An action of the army window for a click on the no-commander entry.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Previous army
summary: An action of the army window that goes to the previous army.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. The window's buttons use GoToPreviousArmy instead. It returns nothing.

label: Select only this unit
summary: Selects only this unit in the army window.
details: Going by its name, other selected units are deselected. Vanilla runs it from a click inside the army window. It returns nothing.

label: The army window itself
summary: The army window object itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on the army window. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Show commanders
summary: Shows the commanders in the army window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from clicks on three buttons of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Show siege
summary: An action of the army window that shows the siege.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. It returns nothing.

label: Show supply trend
summary: Whether the army window should show the supply trend.
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide two widgets of the army window. Going by its name, they show how the army's supply is changing.

label: Split selected in half
summary: Splits the selected units of the army window in half.
details: Going by its name, half of the selection is split off. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Split selected for siege
summary: Splits the selected units of the army window off for a siege.
details: Going by its name, the split-off part is meant for a siege. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Split hired and event troops
summary: Splits the selected hired and event troops off in the army window.
details: Going by its name, the troops split off are the hired ones and those from events. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Stop gathering
summary: Stops the army from gathering.
details: Going by its name, it ends the gathering of the army's troops. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle attach to window
summary: Switches attaching to the army window on or off.
details: Going by its name and IsAttachedToAnyUnit, it flips whether the window is attached to a unit. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle bartering
summary: Switches bartering for the army on or off.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from clicks in the army window, two lines in all. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle looting
summary: Switches looting for the army on or off.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click in the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle raiding
summary: Switches raiding for the army on or off.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from clicks in the army window, two lines in all. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle reorganization window
summary: Opens or closes the reorganization window of the army.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle split army window
summary: Opens or closes the window for splitting the army.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the army window. It returns nothing.

label: The artifact itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact itself.
details: No game file uses it on an artifact. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Can be a holy relic
summary: Whether the artifact can become a holy relic.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the artifact details window.

label: Can benefit
summary: Whether the given character can benefit from the artifact.
details: Going by its name and its one argument only: no game file uses it. The argument is most likely the character; the game does not say. The no-argument CanBenefitPlayer is used in vanilla for the player.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the character to check; not documented.
fields.values: a character

label: Can benefit the player
summary: Whether the player can benefit from the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact details window and in the artifact tooltip to switch between two displays.

label: Can player equip
summary: Whether the player can equip the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in the artifact tooltip, where the negated form shows an extra block. Going by the names, GetCanPlayerEquipDesc is its text counterpart.

label: Can reforge
summary: Whether the given character can reforge the artifact.
details: Vanilla passes the character of the reforge window and uses the result to show and to enable a button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would do the reforging.
fields.values: a character, for example the one of the reforge window

label: Can reforge or repair
summary: Whether the given character can reforge or repair the artifact.
details: Vanilla passes the artifact's owner and uses the result to enable buttons in the artifact, inventory and ledger windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would do it.
fields.values: a character, vanilla uses the artifact's owner

label: Can repair
summary: Whether the given character can repair the artifact.
details: Vanilla passes the character of the reforge window and uses the result to enable a button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would do the repairing.
fields.values: a character, for example the one of the reforge window

label: Custom text
summary: A text made by the named custom localization, run on the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it with 'artifact_rarity_ledger' in the inventory and ledger windows. The name of a custom localization goes in quotes as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The key of the custom localization to run.
fields.values: a key in quotes, such as 'artifact_rarity_ledger'

label: Age
summary: The age of the artifact as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the ledger window. The unit is not given; going by the name it is years.

label: Associated title
summary: The title the artifact is tied to.
details: Vanilla names it in the text 'Inherited along with ...' and uses it as the data context in the ledger. Going by that text, whoever inherits the title also inherits the artifact.

label: Can benefit description
summary: A text describing the requirement for the player to benefit from the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it alone as the text of the artifact-effect requirement tooltip.

label: Can equip description
summary: A text about whether the player can equip the artifact.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the artifact tooltip.

label: Category
summary: The artifact's category as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the artifact tooltip.

label: Creator
summary: The character who created the artifact.
details: Vanilla chains GetName after it in the line 'Creator: ...'. HasCreator tells whether there is one.

label: Culture
summary: The culture of the artifact.
details: Vanilla turns it into a scope and uses it to pick an illustration in the inventory window. Many other game texts use the same name on other things.

label: Description
summary: The artifact's description text.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the artifact details window and in the artifact tooltip.

label: Durability
summary: The artifact's current durability.
details: A fixed-point number. Vanilla converts it to a normal number and uses it as the value of a bar in the reforge and inventory windows, next to GetMaxDurability.

label: Durability tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for the artifact's durability.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the inventory window and the royal court window.

label: Fallback effects
summary: A text listing the effects the artifact gives when its requirements are not met.
details: Vanilla puts it under the heading 'If you do not fulfill the requirements'.

label: Feature text
summary: The text of one named feature of the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in artifact descriptions, for example for the decoration pattern of a hilt, giving the feature type in quotes.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a feature type in quotes, such as 'decoration_pattern'

label: Forgotten soldiers count
summary: The number of 'forgotten soldiers' of the artifact, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'Forgotten Soldiers' in a kill list text. What counts as forgotten is not documented.

label: History
summary: The history of the artifact.
details: Vanilla chains GetEntries after it to fill a list in the artifact details window. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Holy site owner
summary: The holy site that holds the artifact.
details: Vanilla prints its name after 'enshrined at', checks IsValid on it, and sets it as the data context in the ledger.

label: House claimants
summary: The list of houses that claim the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the ledger window. Going by its name, the entries are houses. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: House claimants text
summary: A text listing the houses that claim the artifact.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it.

label: ID
summary: The artifact's id number.
details: Vanilla passes it to open the kill list and the reforge view of that artifact, and prints it in a court scene editor line.

label: Icon
summary: The artifact's icon picture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the inventory and ledger windows. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Icon frame
summary: The frame number of the artifact's icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as the frame of icons in the inventory window, which picks one picture out of a strip of pictures.

label: Holy relic requirements text
summary: A text explaining whether the artifact is a holy relic for the given faith.
details: Vanilla gives it the player's faith and shows the result as the holy relic requirements breakdown.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a faith, for example the player's faith

label: Kills
summary: The list of kills recorded on the artifact.
details: Vanilla only asks whether it has items, to show or hide a part of the artifact details window and the ledger. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Maximum durability
summary: The artifact's maximum durability.
details: A fixed-point number. Vanilla converts it to a normal number and uses it as the maximum of the durability bar.

label: Modifier effects
summary: A text listing the modifiers the artifact gives.
details: Vanilla shows it in the artifact details window and in the artifact effect text.

label: Name
summary: The artifact's name.
details: Used very often in game texts, for example in task contract and memory descriptions. Going by the pair of names, this is the version with a hover tooltip, and GetNameNoTooltip the one without.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The artifact's name, going by its name without a hover tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tournament reward toast and in the holy site's enshrine tooltip texts.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the artifact.
details: Vanilla chains more functions after it, such as the owner's custom text, titled first name and culture, and passes the owner to other functions. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Personal claimants
summary: The list of characters who personally claim the artifact.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Player modifier effects
summary: A text listing the modifiers the artifact gives the player.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. GetModifierEffects is the one vanilla uses.

label: Rarity
summary: The artifact's rarity, as text.
details: Vanilla's inventory texts write it before the artifact's type or slot type: "[rarity] [type]".

label: Rarity and slot type
summary: A text with the artifact's rarity and its slot type.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the interaction templates, the inventory window and the situation list.

label: Rarity and type
summary: A text with the artifact's rarity and its type.
details: Vanilla shows it as text and as a tooltip in the artifact details and inventory windows.

label: Rarity color
summary: The color that stands for the artifact's rarity.
details: A four-value vector (CVector4f), used by vanilla as a color. Vanilla uses it as the color of widgets and as a text tint in the inventory window.

label: Rarity (full)
summary: The artifact's rarity as text, in a longer form than GetRarity.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets after the name in the holy site's artifact slot line. How it differs from GetRarity is not documented; 'longer' is a guess from the name.

label: Reforge or repair tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for reforging or repairing the artifact, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the artifact's owner and shows the result as a tooltip or text in the artifact, inventory and ledger windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character who would reforge or repair.
fields.values: a character, vanilla uses the artifact's owner

label: Reforge tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for reforging the artifact, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the character of the reforge window and shows the result as a tooltip there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example the one of the reforge window

label: Repair tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for repairing the artifact, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the character of the reforge window and shows the result as a tooltip there.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example the one of the reforge window

label: Sanctified for faiths
summary: The faiths the artifact is sanctified for.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. Its return type is not registered in the game's data.

label: Slot type
summary: The name of the slot type of the artifact, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the inventory texts: after the artifact's rarity ('[rarity] [slot type]') and on its own. Going by its name, the slot type says which inventory slot the artifact goes into.

label: Artifact type
summary: The name of the artifact's type, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in the inventory texts: after the artifact's rarity ('[rarity] [type]') and on its own. It differs from the slot type, which has its own function.

label: Years until decay
summary: The number of years until the artifact decays.
details: Vanilla prints it followed by the word 'years'.

label: Years until house claim
summary: The number of years until a house claim on the artifact, for the given character.
details: Vanilla passes the artifact's owner and prints the number in brackets after the owner's house name, followed by 'years'. What exactly the number counts down to is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the claim is checked for.
fields.values: a character, vanilla uses the artifact's owner

label: Has can-benefit rule
summary: Whether the artifact has a rule about who can benefit from it.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses it in the artifact effect text to choose between two localization keys, but no line names it as a function of its own.

label: Has claim
summary: Whether the given character has a claim on the artifact.
details: Vanilla passes the player and combines it with a check that the owner is not the local player, to show a part of the artifact and inventory windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a character, for example the player

label: Has creator
summary: Whether the artifact has a creator.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the artifact tooltip.

label: Has feature
summary: Whether the artifact has the given feature.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. The argument is most likely a feature key; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the feature to look for; not documented.
fields.values: a feature key

label: Has feature of type
summary: Whether the artifact has a feature of the given type.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. The argument is most likely a feature type; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the feature type to look for; not documented.
fields.values: a feature type

label: Has imminent house claim
summary: Whether a house claim on the artifact is about to start for the given character.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla passes the artifact's owner and uses it to show a block in the artifact tooltip. GetYearsUntilHouseClaim is probably the matching time, but the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the claim is checked for.
fields.values: a character, vanilla uses the artifact's owner

label: Is active holy relic for
summary: Whether the artifact is the active holy relic for the given holy site.
details: Vanilla passes a holy site and shows a part of the ledger window when this is false.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a holy site

label: Is court artifact
summary: Whether the artifact is a court artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in the inventory window, and in a text that says 'Displayed' for court artifacts and 'Equipped' for the others.

label: Is durability low
summary: Whether the artifact's durability is low.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the artifact details window and to switch between two displays in the inventory window. The limit is not shown.

label: Is holy relic for
summary: Whether the artifact is a holy relic for the given faith.
details: Vanilla passes a faith, for example the faith of the holder of a holy site's county, and uses the result in holy site texts and windows.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a faith

label: Is inventory artifact
summary: Whether the artifact is in a character's inventory.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it.

label: Is owned by a character
summary: Whether a character owns the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the ledger window.

label: Is owned by a holy site
summary: Whether a holy site owns the artifact.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ledger window, also combined with a check that the owner holds titles.

label: Is sanctified for
summary: Whether the artifact is sanctified for the given faith.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it. The argument is most likely a faith; the game does not say.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Presumably the faith to check; not documented.
fields.values: a faith

label: Is unique
summary: Whether the artifact is unique.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts of the inventory and ledger windows.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the artifact object is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the notification templates only when the artifact is valid. It is used a lot in total, on many other types too.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the artifact into a script scope.
details: Going by its name and its Scope return type. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types, where more functions such as ScriptValue(...) are chained after it.

label: Open rename window
summary: Opens the window for renaming the artifact.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button in the artifact details window. It returns nothing.

label: The artifact itself
summary: The artifact itself, for passing it as an argument to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it, for example, to functions that select an artifact or show its equipped slot.

label: Should decay
summary: Whether the artifact should decay.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it.

label: The claim itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact claim itself.
details: No game file uses it on an artifact claim. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact an artifact claim is about.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context in the inventory and royal court windows, so the artifact's values can be read there.

label: Is house claim
summary: Whether the claim is a claim of a house.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the inventory window.

label: Is personal claim
summary: Whether the claim is a personal claim of a character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the inventory window.

label: The claim itself
summary: The artifact claim itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on an artifact claim. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types.

label: The claims list itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the claims list itself.
details: No game file uses it on the claims list. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Claims
summary: The list of artifact claims.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the claims list in the inventory window, and checks whether it has items to enable a tab and pick its tooltip.

label: Number of claims
summary: The number of artifact claims in the list.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it.

label: Sort options
summary: The list of ways the claims can be sorted.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the sort drop-down in the inventory and royal court windows.

label: Selected sort option
summary: The position of the chosen sort option in the sort options.
details: A pair of whole numbers (CVector2i). Vanilla uses it as the selected index of the sort drop-down in the inventory and royal court windows.

label: Is sort order descending
summary: Whether the claims are sorted in descending order.
details: Vanilla turns it into a frame number (1 or 2) for an icon in the inventory window. Going by the name, the icon shows the sort direction.

label: The claims list itself
summary: The claims list itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on the claims list. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types.

label: Sort claims
summary: Sorts the claims by the chosen option.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it when the selection of the sort drop-down changes, in the inventory and royal court windows. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle sort order
summary: Flips the sort order of the claims between ascending and descending.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button in the inventory and royal court windows. It returns nothing.

label: The details view itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact details view itself.
details: No game file uses it on the details view. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Close
summary: Closes the artifact details view.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the artifact details window; going by its name, the close button. It returns nothing.

label: Artifact
summary: The artifact shown in the artifact details view.
details: Vanilla sets it as the data context of the artifact details window, so the artifact's values can be read there.

label: Claimants
summary: The list of claimants of the artifact shown.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the artifact details window and counts its entries in the title 'Claimants (n)' of a tab.

label: The details view itself
summary: The artifact details view itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on the details view. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types.

label: The helper window itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact helper window itself.
details: No game file uses it on this window. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Can create
summary: Whether the artifact helper window can create an artifact now.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the create button, and its negation to show a widget of the window. What it requires is not documented.

label: Create artifact
summary: Creates an artifact from the choices made in the helper window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the artifact helper window. It returns nothing.

label: Artifact types
summary: The list of artifact types to pick from in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the artifact helper window.

label: Artifact visual types
summary: The list of artifact visual types to pick from in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the artifact helper window.

label: Entities list
summary: The list of entities shown in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the artifact helper window. Going by the three category buttons (all, artifacts, visual type), the list follows the chosen category.

label: Selected asset
summary: The asset chosen in the helper window, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as plain text in the artifact helper window.

label: Selected type
summary: The artifact type chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla chains GetKey after it and shows the key as plain text. HasSelectedType is used to show a part of the window.

label: Selected visual type
summary: The artifact visual type chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla chains GetKey after it and shows the key as plain text. HasSelectedVisualType is used to show a part of the window.

label: Has selected asset
summary: Whether an asset is chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the artifact helper window.

label: Has selected type
summary: Whether an artifact type is chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the artifact helper window.

label: Has selected visual type
summary: Whether an artifact visual type is chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the artifact helper window.

label: Is asset selected
summary: Whether the given asset is the one chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla passes the text of a list row and uses the result as the pressed state of that row's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a text, vanilla passes the list row's own text

label: Is entities category
summary: Whether the given category is the one chosen for the entities list.
details: Vanilla checks 'all', 'artifacts' and 'visual_type' and uses the result as the pressed state of three buttons.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: 'all', 'artifacts' or 'visual_type' (the ones vanilla uses)

label: Is type selected
summary: Whether the given artifact type is the one chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla passes the type of a list row and uses the result as the pressed state of that row's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an artifact type, vanilla uses the row's own type

label: Is visual type selected
summary: Whether the given visual type is the one chosen in the helper window.
details: Vanilla passes the visual type of a list row and uses the result as the pressed state of that row's button.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an artifact visual type, vanilla uses the row's own type

label: Choose asset
summary: Chooses the given asset in the helper window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a list row, passing the row's text. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a text, vanilla passes the list row's own text

label: Filter changed
summary: Reacts to the filter text of the helper window changing.
details: Vanilla runs it when text is edited in a box and when return is pressed there. Going by its name, it updates the list for the new filter. It returns nothing.

label: Choose type
summary: Chooses the given artifact type in the helper window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a list row, passing the row's type. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an artifact type, vanilla uses the row's own type

label: Choose visual type
summary: Chooses the given visual type in the helper window.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click on a list row, passing the row's visual type. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an artifact visual type, vanilla uses the row's own type

label: The helper window itself
summary: The artifact helper window itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on this window. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types.

label: Set entities category
summary: Sets which category the helper window's entities list shows.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from three buttons with 'all', 'artifacts' and 'visual_type'. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: 'all', 'artifacts' or 'visual_type' (the ones vanilla uses)

label: Update entities
summary: Refreshes the helper window's entities list.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla runs it from a click in the artifact helper window. It returns nothing.

label: The history itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact history itself.
details: No game file uses it on the history. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: History entries
summary: The list of entries in an artifact's history.
details: The only matching line is Artifact.GetHistory.GetEntries, used as the data model of a list in the artifact details window. That the history there is an ArtifactHistory is an inference, since GetHistory's return type is not registered.

label: The history itself
summary: The artifact history itself, for passing it on.
details: Going by its name only: no game file uses it on the history. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to other types.

label: The kill list window itself (access)
summary: Going by its name, a way to get the artifact kill list window itself.
details: No game file uses it on this window. The lines of the same name in vanilla belong to another type (PdxGuiWidget). The game documents nothing more.

label: Close
summary: Closes the artifact kill list window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click on a button of the kill list window; going by its name, the close button. It returns nothing.
